home.aboutLead: We believe in a more united, inclusive and prosperous region
home.aboutBody: The Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC) is the region's largest space for political, economic and cultural integration. We are 33 countries working for dialogue, development, sovereignty, peace and international cooperation, driving joint solutions to the challenges we share.
home.whatWeDoBody: CELAC brings together the efforts of Latin American and Caribbean States to jointly respond to our region's challenges: sustainable development, environmental protection, food security, education, public health and democratic strengthening. We are a space for dialogue and cooperation that puts the well-being of our peoples at the center.
home.allianceDesc: Cooperation with regions and organizations around the world to drive development, innovation and economic cooperation projects.

home.faqIntro: CELAC is a regional integration space that promotes dialogue, cooperation and development among the countries of Latin America and the Caribbean. For those looking to learn more about how it works, here we answer some of the most frequently asked questions.
home.faqA1: Its main function is to strengthen regional integration, drive cooperation and build a common voice for Latin America and the Caribbean on issues of global interest.
home.faqA2: It is made up of 33 sovereign countries of Latin America and the Caribbean. It brings together all the nations of the region, with the goal of acting in a coordinated way that respects the sovereignty of each State.
home.faqQ3: How does its Pro Tempore Presidency work?
home.faqA3: The Pro Tempore Presidency is assigned each year to a member country. That country is responsible for coordinating meetings, agendas, projects and declarations during its term, ensuring continuity of regional work.
home.faqContactBody: Write to us and we'll help answer your questions about CELAC.

queEsCelac.eyebrow: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States
queEsCelac.title: What is CELAC?
queEsCelac.lead: A mechanism for regional dialogue and integration created on December 3, 2011, bringing together 33 sovereign States of Latin America and the Caribbean to advance political, economic, social and cultural unity.
queEsCelac.missionText: To represent the collective interests of its member States, protect its citizens, and serve as a gateway for their regional integration.
queEsCelac.visionText: To build a region where cooperation, science, education and innovation play a key role in a more inclusive and sustainable future.
queEsCelac.principlesSubtitle: The pillars that sustain the joint work of the member States.
queEsCelac.principle1Desc: Permanent diplomatic dialogue among the countries of the region.
queEsCelac.principle2Desc: Respect for diversity and regional unity as a shared path.
queEsCelac.principle3Desc: Joint work on social development, education, energy, environment and finance.
queEsCelac.principle4Desc: One single voice for Latin America and the Caribbean before other global blocs.
queEsCelac.whyBody: CELAC was created to provide a space of its own where all Latin American and Caribbean States can dialogue as equals, fostering integration as a tool for sustainable development.
queEsCelac.howSubtitle: Five bodies, from the highest political decision-making level to specialized technical work.
queEsCelac.how1Title: Summit of Heads of State and Government
queEsCelac.how1Desc: CELAC's highest political decision-making body, where the community's priorities and directions are defined.
queEsCelac.how2Title: Meeting of Ministers of Foreign Affairs
queEsCelac.how2Desc: Follows up on the Summit's mandates and prepares the decisions later elevated to Heads of State.
queEsCelac.how3Desc: Coordinates the working agenda among the focal points designated by each member State.
queEsCelac.how4Desc: Sectoral spaces that address specific agenda items: energy, education, health, environment and more.
queEsCelac.how5Desc: CELAC's Quartet —past, present and incoming presidency, plus the Pro Tempore Secretariat— together with CARICOM's Pro Tempore Presidency.
queEsCelac.timelineSubtitle: A timeline of CELAC's construction, from 2008 to 2025.
queEsCelac.milestone1Desc: Initial agreement to strengthen regional integration among Latin American and Caribbean countries.
queEsCelac.milestone2Desc: Convergence of the Rio Group and the Latin America and Caribbean Summit (CALC).
queEsCelac.milestone3Desc: Adoption of the Caracas Declaration and formal creation of CELAC.
queEsCelac.milestone4Desc: CELAC establishes itself as a strategic partner of the European Union.
queEsCelac.milestone6Desc: Emphasis on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
queEsCelac.milestone7Desc: Reaffirmation of the commitment to regional integration.
queEsCelac.milestone8Desc: Priorities on peace, food sovereignty and energy transition.

paisesMiembros.title: Member States
paisesMiembros.lead: The Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC) is made up of 33 sovereign countries across Latin America and the Caribbean. It is a forum that brings together the entire region, without including the United States or Canada.
paisesMiembros.langTitle: CELAC brings together countries with five predominant official languages
paisesMiembros.achievements1: Throughout its existence, the 33 nations of this political dialogue forum have signed 164 bilateral and multilateral free trade agreements. CELAC's main achievement has been advancing the gradual process of regional integration, balancing unity with the political, economic, social and cultural diversity of the 620 million inhabitants of Latin America and the Caribbean. The mechanism has driven improvements in education through cooperation initiatives that share experiences on bringing the knowledge society to the wider population, and it has notably strengthened ties with the Caribbean — particularly on climate change and disaster response — as well as extra-regional relationships.
paisesMiembros.achievements2: In addition, for the first time and by unanimous decision, Colombia was elected to hold CELAC's pro tempore presidency for 2025, reaffirming Colombia's interest in strengthening and promoting the integration of Latin America and the Caribbean. Colombia is therefore currently part of CELAC's Troika (current, previous and upcoming pro tempore presidency) as the incoming PPT.
paisesMiembros.achievements3: During Mexico's pro tempore presidency in 2021, the Climate Adaptation and Comprehensive Natural Disaster Response Fund (FACRID) was established at CELAC's VI Summit of Heads of State and Government, held on September 18, 2021, to mobilize financial resources from voluntary contributions by CELAC Member States and extra-regional partners to support projects and activities for disaster prevention, reduction, mitigation, response and recovery in the region. It is administered by the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC). Colombia joined FACRID on November 14, 2023, as a member of its Governing Council, reaffirming its strong commitment to disaster prevention and mitigation in the region.
paisesMiembros.achievements4: On April 26, 2023, the Acapulco Declaration was signed between Colombia, Cuba and Mexico to formalize negotiations for the creation of the Latin American and Caribbean Medicines Agency (AMLAC), aiming to achieve health self-sufficiency and access to medicines and medical devices through shared health regulation strategies among the countries of the region.
